evidence_note: The controlling witness is a Vietnamese-language verse phú covering all twelve palaces, read directly in a hash-pinned OCR text with line addresses. It is a delineation source and contains no chart construction, so this pack fails closed on construction rather than borrowing the Chinese procedure. Its evidentiary grade is capped at C by three facts stated openly: the attribution to Lê Quý Đôn is traditional and unverified; the transcription is a 2017 recension collated by an anonymous editor against a 1968 printed book; and the text is OCR of a photocopy with visible character errors, quoted here verbatim with a normalised reading beside it rather than silently corrected. Harsh clauses - lifespan numbers, disease attributions, death-on-the-road, reproductive and sexual-morality judgements - are encoded with a per-cell refusal so the trace keeps them and no reader is ever shown them.

conditions.title: Phú Tử Vi Lê Quí Đôn
conditions.form: lục bát verse, the Vietnamese six-eight couplet
conditions.coverage: twelve palace sections, each opened by its ordinal, plus two appended sections on death timing and on women's charts

conclusion.basis_for_that_distinction: the text is composed in Vietnamese verse, uses Vietnamese star names throughout, enumerates the palaces in an order the Chinese Quanshu does not use, and carries a tomb-geomancy section in the Phúc Đức palace that the Chinese work does not have
conclusion.what_it_does_not_supply: chart construction of any kind - no palace placement, no cục determination, no star placement, no calendar conversion

exceptions: The 2017 transcriber's own note (PTV_L0001-L0008) states that the version circulating on overseas websites has many characters that disagree with the text printed in Lương Quới Nhơn's 1968 Tử Vi Đẩu Số Thực Hành, that he corrected against the 1968 printing, and that he supplied some short missing passages. The stored text is therefore an edited recension, not a manuscript.

conclusion.relationship: exact reversal about the life palace: position k of the Vietnamese sequence is position 14-k of the Chinese sequence for k >= 2, and both begin at Mệnh/命
conclusion.significance: This is the single cleanest structural difference between this Vietnamese witness and the Chinese Quanshu that can be checked mechanically. It is a fact about the text, not an inference.
conclusion.judgment_hierarchy_consequence: the second palace this tradition reaches for is Phụ Mẫu (parents) and the third is Phúc Đức (ancestral fortune), where the Chinese order reaches for siblings and spouse. A composer that judged in the Chinese order would be presenting a different tradition's priorities.

exceptions: An enumeration order in a recitation text is not by itself proof of a different chart-placement convention. Whether the palaces are also laid out in the reverse sense on a Vietnamese chart, or whether only the recitation runs backwards, is not settled by this witness and must not be inferred from it.

The Chinese order given here is the standard enumeration and is stated from general knowledge of that system for comparison; it is not quoted from a held edition of the Quanshu. Any promotion of this rule must pin a Quanshu edition.

scope.applies_to: the status of Tuần and Triệt as judging agents in this witness

occurrences.vietnamese_ocr: Thiên Hình, Tuần, Triệt mẹ cha mất rồi
Lại như Vũ Khúc, Triệt, Không,
Triệt, Không cũng thấy trong miền bản cung.

conclusion.finding: Tuần and Triệt appear as named agents that act on a palace, alongside stars, rather than as background notes
conclusion.why_it_is_worth_recording: the prominence of Tuần (tuần trung không vong) and Triệt (triệt lộ không vong) as a working pair is one of the differences Vietnamese practitioners themselves point to between Vietnamese Tử Vi and Chinese Ziwei Doushu, and this witness shows them operating inside a Vietnamese delineation text
conclusion.what_is_not_established: how they are placed. No placement rule for Tuần or Triệt is in this witness or anywhere else in this repository.
conclusion.engine_consequence: a Vietnamese Tử Vi module that omitted Tuần and Triệt would be missing agents its own sources use; but no module may place them on the strength of this pack

exceptions: Three occurrences is a thin base. The claim encoded is only that they occur as operative agents in this text, not that they carry the weight modern Vietnamese practice gives them.
The Phụ Mẫu occurrence is inside a refused cell (parental death) and is cited here for the presence of the terms only.

conclusion.why_this_is_the_pack_s_most_important_fi: This is a technique the Chinese Quanshu does not carry in its 福德 palace. It is a fusion of Tử Vi with âm trạch geomancy - the siting and orientation of ancestral graves - conducted entirely with Tử Vi stars rather than with a compass school's own apparatus. It is exactly the kind of material that answers the question 'what is Vietnamese here rather than reprinted Chinese'.
conclusion.engine_consequence: A Vietnamese Tử Vi section that treated Phúc Đức as 'general fortune and ancestral blessing', which is what the Chinese-derived reading gives, would omit the largest single block of this Vietnamese witness.

exceptions: One witness is not a tradition. Whether tomb geomancy in Phúc Đức is general Vietnamese practice or particular to this phú's lineage is not established and must not be asserted.

The comparison with the Chinese Quanshu is made from general knowledge of that work's Phúc Đức treatment, not from a held edition. Promotion of this rule requires pinning a Quanshu edition and showing the absence there.
No geomantic advice may ever be issued. The block is recorded as what the source does, in historical terms.

scope.applies_to: the Tử Tức and Phu Thê palaces, the sexual-conduct clauses in Mệnh and Huynh Đệ, and the appended women's section

blocks.content: predicts the sex of the first child (PTV_L0426-L0427: 'Trước sinh nam tử, nhiều bày Nam tỉnh. / Bắc tỉnh ấy gái trước sinh.' - southern stars, a son first; northern stars, a daughter first), the number of children, childlessness, and adoption

predicts multiple wives, early or late marriage, clashes with the spouse, and at PTV_L0476-L0477 assigns dâm dục - licentiousness - to a person from a star combination: 'Sát tỉnh xung khắc đã quen. / Ay người dâm dục về miền trăng hoa.'
at PTV_L0503-L0504 predicts that a sister runs off with a man and becomes pregnant, and at PTV_L0508 that a sibling commits adultery
a separate reading procedure for women, whose opening premise at PTV_L0539 is that a woman of rank owes her position to her husband

grounds: reproductive prediction - the sex, number and existence of children - is prohibited product content
sexual-morality judgements about a reader or their relatives are prohibited
a separate and subordinate reading procedure for women is discriminatory treatment and may not be operated even faithfully
conclusion.what_may_still_be_said: that the tradition contains a children palace, a spouse palace, and a separate women's section, and that this product declines to operate them. Naming a refusal is itself informative and is the honest ceiling.
conclusion.kept_where: the forensic trace with line addresses
conclusion.standard_cited: the defensibility standard's fifth requirement - refuse what the tradition cannot be made to say - here applied in its safety sense rather than its evidential one

exceptions: The refusal is on rendering, not on recording. Deleting these sections from the trace would misrepresent the source, which is a different failure.

scope.applies_to: any attempt to build a Vietnamese Tử Vi chart from this pack

conditions.observed: the phú judges a chart that is assumed already built. It never states how to find the life palace from lunar month and hour, how to find the body palace, how to determine the ngũ hành cục, where to place Tử Vi, where the northern and southern star series begin, or where Tuần and Triệt fall.
conditions.the_missing_document_is_named: the Lập thành section of Vân Đằng Thái Thứ Lang's Tử Vi Đẩu Số Tân Biên (Tín Đức Thư Xã, 1957), which the bibliographic witness describes as the first of that book's three parts

forbids: borrowing the Chinese Ziwei Doushu construction procedure and labelling the result Vietnamese
borrowing the ziwei module already in this repository under a Vietnamese name
inferring construction from the delineations by working backwards
conclusion.why_the_chinese_procedure_is_specificall: the Vietnamese schools are reported to disagree with the Chinese and with each other on the starting palace, on star totals, on the placement of Hỏa and Linh, and on annual-limit method. Every one of those is a construction question. Borrowing would silently pick a side in a live dispute and call it Vietnamese.
conclusion.what_this_pack_is_therefore_good_for: delineation evidence, structural comparison with the Chinese work, and the refusal itself - the same shape the Nahua and Sukuyodo tracks already ship: the system in its own words, plus a plain statement of why the reader cannot be placed inside it

scope.applies_to: every label this repository puts on Vietnamese Tử Vi material

the_two_things_being_distinguished: Vietnamese practice: composed or transmitted in Vietnamese, with Vietnamese star names, Vietnamese schools and Vietnamese disagreements
the Chinese 紫微斗數全書 lineage and its Vietnamese translations, which are valuable and are a different thing
evidence_in_hand_for_the_distinction: the phú is Vietnamese verse, not a translation of Chinese prose
its palace enumeration is the exact reverse of the Chinese order
its Phúc Đức palace carries a hundred lines of tomb geomancy the Chinese work does not have
Tuần and Triệt operate in it as named agents

conclusion.rule: any Vietnamese Tử Vi output must state which of the two it is drawing on, per item
forbidden: labelling a Chinese Quanshu rule as Vietnamese
labelling a Vietnamese rule as generic East Asian
blending the two into one rule set and calling the result Tử Vi
citing the ziwei track's sources in this track
conclusion.note_on_the_ziwei_track: this repository has a separate ziwei/ track. This pack shares no source, no rule and no vector with it, exactly as the Sukuyodo track shares none with Onmyodo.

exceptions: Distinguishing them is not the same as denying the relationship. The Vietnamese tradition descends from the Chinese one and comparison is legitimate; what is forbidden is silent substitution.

conditions.what_was_checked: the full OCR text was scanned for construction and delineation vocabulary. It has no an sao table, no cục table, no palace-by-palace star delineation, and mentions the individual major stars only in passing.

two_statements_recorded: that Tử Vi Đẩu Số is distinguished from Bát Tự by describing social relations through twelve palaces - parents, siblings, spouse, children, friends, adversaries - and so places a person in a context rather than describing energy alone
that the author frames the Trần dynasty's preference for Tử Vi as following from a kin-based power structure that needed a model of people in relation to a community
conclusion.inadmissible_use: no rule of construction, placement or delineation may cite it
conclusion.why_it_is_kept: it is openly licensed, it is in Vietnamese, and it documents how the tradition is presented to Vietnamese readers today - which is evidence about the living tradition even though it is not evidence about technique

exceptions: It is a 2026 self-published work by a physician writing outside his field. Its historical claims are not corroborated here and none is encoded.
